report.question: Developer request: bring the compiled donor’s dash into JUJUMP while retaining its timing and the platformer’s own physics. Recover a NEW standalone motion candidate. Prefer a compact experiment program to inspect the binary and chosen function bodies and run a checkpoint-bound controlled memory comparison. Choose hypotheses, code and inputs yourself. In a later model turn, use the actual result to choose evidence or a follow-up. Select inspected code and execution evidence, submit source, inspect real development first divergences and revise if needed. Use cooldown and remaining as the timer state field names for the current recipient instrumentation; infer their values and rules. Freeze a development-passed candidate and call separate acceptance, then conclude with actual experiment citations. The host checks the recipient only after recovery; you cannot claim recipient success. No pre-existing recovered implementation is available. Report incomplete work honestly; mapped fields, ABI, evaluators and recipient adapter are human assistance.

Conclusion from actual recorded evidence:

Observations:
- Inspected compiled donor `152d44c6e...` via `binary:func11` ($update) — code-inspection milestone satisfied.
- Controlled identical-input experiments completed:
  - `experiment-174c8915-6245-4528-8064-f77a045f3c5a` (X-press / dash): 30 updates, 8 activeUpdates, `dash-start` at elapsedFrame 1 with `cooldown:25, remaining:7, dx:7.5`, `dash-end` at elapsedFrame 8, lastTimers `cooldown:3, remaining:0`. Control vs intervention identical (reproducibility control).
  - `experiment-66e3cd51-5731-4611-be10-a43cf9d4c451` (idle baseline): 0 activeUpdates, no events, timers stay 0.
- Selected recovery evidence `selection-1` binds `binary:func11` + both experiments for dash-motion candidate scope: 8-frame dash, cooldown 25, remaining 7.

Interpretation:
- X triggers timed dash motion with exact start/end events; idle does not. Timing values inferred from traces, not yet proven causal via memory perturbation.
- No controlled branch memory comparison (`compare_branches`), no submitted / frozen / accepted component completed in this run.

Remaining / inconclusive:
- Branch-comparison, development-pass, freeze, and separate acceptance all unfinished. No standalone candidate claimed; no recipient success claimed.
- Direction, distance accumulation, cooldown blocking rules, and bytecode causality remain unverified; require new branch-perturbation and development/acceptance work.

tools.name: execution
tools.description: Observe or reconstruct checkpoint state, read compact experiment evidence and selectively capture actual images.

tools.name: read_checkpoint
tools.description: Observe an existing checkpoint without advancing or changing main. Return typed target handles for human-mapped hints and requested raw memory watches. Handles bind address, type, previous bytes and checkpoint identity; raw watch names are hypotheses.

tools.name: read_experiment
tools.description: Read a bounded window from an immutable completed experiment artifact. Large complete traces stay in the evidence store; this returns at most four requested frames and endpoint observations.

tools.name: capture_experiment
tools.description: Reconstruct and verify one completed experiment endpoint, then selectively capture its actual PNG. Image identity retains session, branch, frame and source artifact. Counts against the same four-image investigation budget; requestId is idempotent.

tools.name: session_observe
tools.description: Observe the current persistent branch without advancing; include bounded typed memory watches. Motion fields are HUMAN-MAPPED assistance.

branchId.description: Identity of an existing branch for observation or execution. main is the initial branch.

tools.name: session_advance
tools.description: Continue this persistent branch with held inputs at 60 Hz, preserving prior state. Checkpoints here are observation labels; use checkpoint_state for a reusable branch point. The initial branch is main. X=1 starts/dashes; left=16, right=32, up=64, down=128. Frames and output are bounded.

branchId.description: Identity of an existing branch for observation or execution. main is the initial branch.

tools.name: checkpoint_state
tools.description: Record a reusable checkpoint bound to cartridge and runtime identity. Restoration replays inputs and edits into a clean instance and verifies frame, memory, framebuffer and host-storage hashes. Private globals are reconstructed, not copied.

branchId.description: Identity of an existing branch for observation or execution. main is the initial branch.

tools.name: session_reset
tools.description: Reset only this branch to a clean cartridge instance, including private globals and host storage.

branchId.description: Identity of an existing branch for observation or execution. main is the initial branch.

tools.name: run_original
tools.description: Run a controlled experiment from fresh cartridge, memory, and empty storage. Each step holds a gamepad mask for fixed 60 Hz updates. Returns checkpoint hashes, visible text, grouped sprite coordinates, requested read-only memory watches, and motion fields from the host's HUMAN-MAPPED, hash-guarded donor registry: world position, direction, remaining active ticks, cooldown, sourceBodyWidth. Null motion means unavailable outside gameplay. The agent does not discover this registry mapping. Use world position to distinguish player movement from camera motion. Watches read little-endian numeric values at absolute byte addresses; use [] when unused. X=1 starts/dashes; Z=2; left=16; right=32; up=64; down=128. OR bits to combine; 0 releases. Maximum 12 checkpoints, 1,800 total frames, and 64 watched values. No source or filesystem access.

tools.name: memory
tools.description: Specialized low-level typed memory and branch tools. Complete experiments normally use run_experiment instead.

tools.name: read_memory
tools.description: Observe the current persistent branch without advancing; include bounded typed memory watches. Motion fields are HUMAN-MAPPED assistance.

branchId.description: Identity of an existing branch for observation or execution. main is the initial branch.

tools.name: write_memory
tools.description: Apply up to eight finite typed writes to an experimental checkpoint branch. Writes to main are forbidden. Records the previous value, rounded new value, address, frame and hypothesis. Code bytes remain immutable. A trapped branch must reset before advancing.

branchId.description: Identity of an existing branch for observation or execution. main is the initial branch.

tools.name: diff_memory
tools.description: Compare up to 4096 bytes as typed values between two observation IDs from this session. Returns absolute candidate addresses and changes, capped at 64. Reconstructs each observation by verified replay. Changes alone are correlation, not inferred names.

tools.name: fork_checkpoint
tools.description: Restore a checkpoint into a new independent experimental branch. main remains unchanged. Give the new branch a short lowercase identity; use the returned identity in later commands.

branchId.description: A NEW unused branch name, such as control or variant. Never use main or any already-created branch. This is the name to CREATE, not the checkpoint source.

tools.name: compare_branches
tools.description: Advance two branches forked from the same checkpoint with exactly the same inputs. The control must have no additional writes. Prior input histories and elapsed frames must match. Observe actual motion, memory and rendering differences; mutations alone are not proof of a field meaning. At most 600 frames total.

controlBranchId.description: Identity of an existing branch for observation or execution. main is the initial branch.

experimentalBranchId.description: Identity of an existing branch for observation or execution. main is the initial branch.

tools.name: capture_frame
tools.description: Capture the current native framebuffer as a real PNG and send it alongside structured evidence to the model. Select only informative frames: at most four images per investigation. The image retains session, branch, frame, palette and hashes.

branchId.description: Identity of an existing branch for observation or execution. main is the initial branch.

tools.name: static
tools.description: Inspect compiled WASM code, direct call graphs, evidence-linked names and actual scalar writers.

tools.name: list_functions
tools.description: List generated function names, signatures, exports, WAT locations, and counts of direct calls and memory instructions in the pinned cartridge. Function indices include imports. Page with nextIndex; names are not recovered source names.

tools.name: inspect_function
tools.description: Inspect one function by index from list_functions. Returns direct callers/callees and up to 100 WAT lines with call sites and memory load/store offsets in that window. startLine is relative to the function, starting at 1. Indirect calls are marked unresolved. A memory offset is added to a runtime base address; it is not necessarily an absolute address. This is disassembly, not recovered source.

tools.name: decompile_function
tools.description: Read bounded WABT C-like pseudocode for an agent-selected function index. This derived interpretation is not original source. Page relative lines as with inspect_function; WAT remains authoritative.

tools.name: call_graph
tools.description: Navigate direct callers or callees of an agent-selected function to depth three, bounded to 60 nodes and 100 edges. Indirect calls remain unresolved. Generated and inferred names are distinct.

tools.name: annotate_function
tools.description: Attach an agent-inferred name and testable interpretation to a function. Include confidence, supported/rejected/unresolved status, and actual observation/comparison/binary evidence IDs from this session. These are annotations, not established source names.

tools.name: trace_writers
tools.description: Trace executed scalar store writers to a selected absolute memory range in a separate instrumented analysis copy restored from a checkpoint. Compare its full observed behavior against the unchanged cartridge for the same inputs. At most 120 frames and 64 hits. Does not implement pausing watchpoints, host writes, SIMD, bulk or atomic write tracing.

tools.name: recovery
tools.description: Select inspected code and execution evidence, develop component candidates, freeze source and run separate acceptance.

tools.name: select_component_evidence
tools.description: Select code YOU inspected and actual session evidence for motion extraction. No pre-existing recovered implementation or curated function list is supplied. The host supplies the motion ABI and human-authored finite development evaluator.

tools.name: submit_component_candidate
tools.description: Submit standalone TypeScript using the selected binary/experiment evidence. Returns real development failures including first divergence for revision. Three attempts maximum. Acceptance is unavailable until a passed candidate is frozen. Export init(config) and step(state,{buttons,sourceBodyWidth},config); output ONLY {ownsMotion,displacement:{x,y},events}. State must expose integer cooldown and remaining fields named by timerFields. Use the original source pixels at fixed 60 Hz; infer defaults from observations. No imports, original binary, runtime, DOM, randomness or networking.

tools.name: freeze_component
tools.description: Freeze the exact source, contract and timer mapping of a development-passed candidate. No revisions are allowed after freezing. Acceptance runs only in a separate subsequent call.

tools.name: accept_component
tools.description: Run separately generated acceptance inputs against the already-frozen candidate. Failure is final for this investigation; no held-out failure is fed to another repair. Finite acceptance is not universal equivalence.
